Rename marketplace to cleanlanguage, add distribution check (#277)

Carry out unit 1 of the plugin distribution plan (TODO 234), which
aligns the repository with the fleet plugin distribution standard,
except its migration note. The maintainer dropped the note (Entry 128),
so plan steps 2 and 3, the plan's smoke-test leg for the note and its
pointer in unit 3 no longer apply.

- The marketplace in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json is renamed from
  jposluns to cleanlanguage, the project name.
- README.md now ends with a newline. No install command is added or
  changed.
- tools/check-plugin-distribution.py, the gate, is a new offline check
  of names, sources, versions and dependencies, with its unit tests in
  tools/test-check-plugin-distribution.py. Its docstring states the
  rules, the output and the exit statuses. Where the CLI's own rule
  cannot be checked offline, the gate refuses. As it decodes, its
  object_pairs_hook `_unique_object` refuses a key repeated among all
  keys of a JSON object, then keeps only the pairs whose key is
  exactly 1 of READ_KEYS, the 6 keys it reads, so another key reaches
  the rest of the gate only when it is repeated, as the key the
  refusal names, and the text it shows of an object value lists only
  those pairs. That hook, `load_json` and READ_KEYS are the core, and
  "the 6" are the keys of READ_KEYS. U, a case, gives the hook every
  letter-case spelling of the 6 and every spelling with any number of
  characters that case mapping maps onto their letters; every
  in-process run fails on an object load_json gives that holds
  another key; and E, a case, runs a copy of the gate only as a
  command, as CI runs it, adds to every object 5 kinds of other
  spelling of the 6 (each other letter case, a trailing space, a
  zero-width space, and U+212A for a k or else U+017F for an s,
  4,571 in all) and a key outside the 6, requires the exit status and
  last line written out in the case, for the repository's files with
  the version their Claude plugin manifest holds, and then the same
  output, and checks its own reach.
- Before it loads the gate, the test compares the sha256 of the gate
  and of tools/skill-version.py, the 2 files of the repository that
  the gate's command executes, with digests written in the test, and
  on a mismatch stops with exit 1 before any case runs. It compiles
  the gate from the bytes it hashed, so no .pyc runs in their place.
  After the comparison it takes its copies of either file from the
  hashed bytes, and in its 2 cases on the repository the gate's own
  read of the extractor must give those bytes, which the gate is then
  given to run. A case shows that an extractor changed after the test
  has loaded the gate does not run in the test's process, in the tree
  setUp writes or on the repository; it plants no earlier change.
  That the other copies come from the hashed bytes, and that the test
  reads neither file from the repository again, rests on review of
  the test, as item 4 below says: a read of either file from the
  repository written at such a site passes every case. Reduced
  coverage: an audit hook that failed such a read, tried on this
  branch, is retired. The case that runs the gate's main on the
  repository compares the last line, as str.splitlines gives it, with
  the OK line and the version of the repository's Claude plugin
  manifest, so a carriage return at the end of that line is not
  caught, as item 6 below says.
  Residual:
  1. The digest shows that the gate and the extractor are, byte for
     byte, the files a reviewer accepted, not that they are right.
     Rightness rests on that review, U, the structural check and the
     outcome cases, and a renewal accepts whatever the diff holds.
  2. The outcome cases see only the inputs they plant and the
     environment they run in. Reviewed code that behaves otherwise on
     other inputs, or that tells a test run from CI's run, is caught
     only by review (RUN: a value-conditional mutant passed both steps
     and every case).
  3. The interpreter, its standard library and the runner image are
     outside the repository and are not pinned. The workflow and
     tools/run_all_checks.sh are outside this test; this note did not
     examine what else holds them.
  4. The test itself is held only by review of its diff. A weakening
     of the digest check or of an outcome case is caught by no case,
     as no test can hold its own text without a further test.
  5. Cost: every edit of either file, a comment included, stops the
     test before any case runs until the digest is renewed, and the
     extractor is shared with other tools, so its edits need this
     renewal too.
  6. test_repository_is_consistent compares the last line of the
     gate's output as str.splitlines gives it, which drops a carriage
     return at the end of the line, so one written there is not caught
     (RUN: a gate that writes one only when its tree holds .github
     passed every case).
- .github/workflows/plugin-distribution.yml runs both on every pull
  request and push to main. It is not a required check.
- tools/run_all_checks.sh mirrors the new workflow; the digest in
  tools/test-run-all-checks.py and the workflow list in
  tools/test-no-qa-labels.py follow.
- Add .github/squash/277.txt as the committed squash message read by
  the Pull request text gate.

The branch merges main at pull request #273, "Write packager outputs
to dist/ only after checks pass". Its only conflict was the
SCRIPT_SHA256 pin in tools/test-run-all-checks.py, since both sides
changed tools/run_all_checks.sh; the pin holds the merged script's
sha256. It later merges main at pull request #268, "Add a CI gate for
pull request texts". Its only conflict was again that pin. Both sides
had changed the script's count of workflows from 17 to 18, which git
merged without a conflict; the merged script now says 19, the count
its test reports, and the pin holds its sha256.

The required check set is unchanged.
